title: ARIA roles must be valid values
summary: An element has a role value that is not a real ARIA role, often a typo. Correct the value or use a native HTML element.
problem: An element has a role attribute whose value is not defined in WAI-ARIA, for example a misspelled role="buton". Browsers ignore an unknown role, so the element loses the meaning you meant to give it.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users hear a plain element instead of the control they should get. A custom button with a typo in its role is not announced as a button at all.
steps: Find the element and the invalid role in the scan result.
Check the spelling against the list of roles in the WAI-ARIA specification. Role names are lowercase.
Use a native element where possible. A <button> needs no role and brings keyboard support.
Remove the role if it was invented or copied from a library that uses its own names.
whyItMatters: A role that does not exist does nothing, and typos are hard to spot in review. This is a WCAG Level A requirement, the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
howToCheck: Re-run the scan, then check the element in your browser's accessibility inspector. It should show a real role such as button.
